title: The affine component square on ordinary derived condensed module categories
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be any morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $P=\pi_0(X)$, $Q=\pi_0(Y)$ be the quotient component spaces [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite], and let $h=\pi_0(f):Q\to P$. Use compatible small-site universes [def-weil-size-convention], the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the component geometric morphisms $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ induced by the relative component lifts [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]. On profinite spaces over $P$ or $Q$ use finite jointly surjective coverings; the geometric morphism associated with $h$ is induced on test objects by $E\mapsto Q\times_P E$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use its pulled-back ring sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its restrictions $\Lambda_P,\Lambda_Q$ on those profinite slice sites. Let $D(-,\Lambda)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor. The natural isomorphism of relative test-object functors $c_{f,E}$ [lem-zl-component-lift-base-change] induces, for the actual inverse-image functors, a natural isomorphism of exact symmetric monoidal functors
$$\theta_f:f^*\pi_X^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_Y^*h^*:D(P,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Lambda).$$
At the coefficient unit, $\theta_f$ is the canonical identification of the two pullbacks of $\Lambda_P$ with $\Lambda_Y$; it respects the tensor comparisons. It is induced by the corresponding isomorphism of exact module-sheaf inverse images applied termwise to complexes and localized at quasi-isomorphisms. It is compatible with identity and composition in $f$, using the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphisms. In particular it restricts to the full subcategories of dualizable objects, where dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation with both triangle identities. No henselian or w-contractibility assumption on $X,Y$ and no discreteness or boundedness assumption on coefficients or complexes is imposed.
